title: The old woman selling rice balls at St. Mary's church
summary: A very old woman with blue eyes sold crispy rice balls outside the church on Sunday mornings.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And everybody knows that's some sort of a call. A Crowleen man passed. Or the old lady passed. How'd you got Crowleen? And on this corner... On the corner of... Charlize and... Ursuline is the... St. Mary's... Catholic Church. And every Sunday morning... There was this old colored lady who was standing there. Real old and small. With a tignon on her head. And... Big, wide, square, typical... Which is a southern man of type. But she was extremely old. But she was very active. She used to be there every morning selling... Carlisle. And most of the sort of... Italians, they'd buy from her. And she's standing on this corner. At least I saw...

The... The... The... The... The... The... The... The... The... The... The... The... Dozens of times. She must have been about... 100 years old then. But she's standing on this corner. And I... Remember getting a good look at her. In fact, I used to buy something from her some time. She gives you three or four of them for a nickel. With little balls of rice... Rice balls. Cooked to a very... Brown... Crispy brown. She never did much smile. She never said nothing. She just stood there. And she was real... Dark. I said... Black. This kinky white hair. I could see a little of it. And she had blue eyes. That's interesting to fascinate me. And later on I found out that... There were quite a few old... Colored people who... As they got older, their eyes turned blue. You know, on the side of the Irish blue. You know, that real sky blue. Did she sing? I mean, did you do any spring fire in her? No, she didn't sing.
